newsitem.title: UK: Dixons sees sales growth of eight percent.
newsitem.headline: Dixons sees sales growth of eight percent.

text.p: British computer and electronics retailer Dixons Group Plc said on Wednesday that same store sales in the first half of the year were up eight percent on the previous period, a figure sustained into the first eight weeks of the second half.

Dixons said pre-tax profits in the first half were 57.5 million pounds ($97.39 million), up 53 percent from a year ago and just ahead of expectations, while the group paid out a dividend of 2.4 pence, up from 2.05 pence previously.

"Christmas trading was highly satisfactory," chairman Sir Stanley Kalms said in a statement, adding that gross margins in the first eight weeks of the second half were "at similar levels year on year," after increasing "slightly" in the first half.

Dixons said its PC World division, which focuses on personal computer sales in out-of-town superstores, saw total sales soar 96 percent from a year ago, or 21 percent stripping out the effect of new selling space.
Dixons said capital expenditure for 1996/97 would be over 100 million pounds and should be similar in 1997/98.

The company said it was not possible to predict at this stage the full effect on its extended warranty business of the British government's proposals to increase insurance premium tax on insurance sold with electrical and other goods. ($1=.5904 Pound)
